teaching_point: Acute urticaria — itchy, raised, blanching wheals with surrounding flare; each wheal fades within 24 h without a mark.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acute-urticaria

teaching_point: Acute urticaria with periorbital angioedema — wheals + itchy swelling = histaminergic; <6 weeks; often post-viral/drug/food; usually no tests needed. Check ABC: no airway/breathing/circulation problem = not anaphylaxis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acute urticaria (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acute-urticaria

teaching_point: Coalescing/annular wheals — shapes change hour to hour; mark and re-check to confirm <24 h duration.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticaria (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acute-urticaria

teaching_point: Chronic spontaneous urticaria — recurrent wheals on most days for >6 weeks with no consistent external trigger.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Spontaneous urticaria (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chronic-spontaneous-urticaria

teaching_point: CSU wheals — manage with daily (not PRN) non-sedating H1 antihistamine, up-dosed to 4× if needed.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Spontaneous urticaria (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chronic-spontaneous-urticaria

teaching_point: Urticaria in skin of colour — erythema subtle; look for raised skin-coloured/violaceous wheals and ask about itch and timing.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticaria in skin of colour (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chronic-urticaria

teaching_point: Wheal in darker skin — palpable oedema is the key sign when redness is hard to see.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Wheal in dark skin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/urticaria-an-overview

teaching_point: Symptomatic dermographism — linear wheals where skin was stroked/scratched; commonest inducible urticaria.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermographism: arm (© Dr Mashihul Hossain) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermographism

teaching_point: Dermographism — firm stroke produces linear weal within minutes, fades in ~30 min; test with blunt object.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermographism (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermographism

teaching_point: Cold urticaria — wheals on cold-exposed skin; warn re cold-water swimming (risk of systemic reaction/drowning).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cold urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cold-urticaria

teaching_point: Ice-cube test — enlarging weal minutes after ice removed confirms cold urticaria.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Enlarging weal 5 minutes later (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cold-urticaria

teaching_point: Cholinergic urticaria — small 2–5 mm itchy wheals with flare after exercise, heat, hot showers or emotion.
dermnet_caption: The transient 5 mm wheals of cholinergic urticaria triggered by exercise
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — The transient 5 mm wheals of cholinergic urticaria triggered by exercise (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cholinergic-urticaria

teaching_point: Delayed pressure urticaria — deep painful swelling 4–8 h after pressure (straps, waistbands, soles); poorer antihistamine response.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pressure urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pressure-urticaria

teaching_point: Solar urticaria — wheals within minutes of sun on usually covered skin; habitually exposed face/hands often spared.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Solar urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/solar-urticaria

teaching_point: Latex contact urticaria — positive immediate wheal on skin testing; contact urticaria is immediate-type, so prick/specific IgE testing (specialist), NOT patch testing.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Latex reaction (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/contact-urticaria

teaching_point: Urticaria pigmentosa (maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis) in a child — red-brown macules/papules; often improves by adolescence.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticaria pigmentosa in a child (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/maculopapular-cutaneous-mastocytosis

teaching_point: Darier sign — rubbing a pigmented lesion produces a wheal and flare within minutes (case scenario-2).
dermnet_caption: Cutaneous mastocytosis in an infant - yellow-brown macules over the chest and back. The chest lesion has urticated 5 minutes after rubbing (Darier sign)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous mastocytosis in an infant - yellow-brown macules over the chest and back. The chest lesion has urticated 5 minutes after rubbing (Darier sign) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mastocytosis

teaching_point: Urticaria pigmentosa — brown spots that urticate; counsel to avoid mast-cell triggers (opioids, NSAIDs, radiocontrast, heat, friction).
dermnet_caption: Urticaria pigmentosa: brown spots that urticate
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticaria pigmentosa: brown spots that urticate (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/maculopapular-cutaneous-mastocytosis

teaching_point: Adult maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis — persistent in adults; check serum tryptase, think systemic mastocytosis; refer.
dermnet_caption: Maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis (urticaria pigmentosa); red-brown maculopapular lesions on the leg
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis (urticaria pigmentosa); red-brown maculopapular lesions on the leg (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mastocytosis

teaching_point: Solitary mastocytoma with Darier sign — toddler; may blister when rubbed; usually resolves.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Darier sign in mastocytoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/mastocytoma

teaching_point: Severe lip angioedema — deep non-pitting swelling; with weals → histaminergic; without weals → consider ACE-i/HAE (bradykinin).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Severe lip angioedema (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angioedema

teaching_point: Eyelid angioedema with urticaria elsewhere — histaminergic angioedema; usually responds to antihistamine.
dermnet_caption: Lid angioedema - there was typical urticaria elsewhere on the body
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lid angioedema - there was typical urticaria elsewhere on the body (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angioedema

teaching_point: Angioedema of the hand — limb swellings without weals and with abdominal attacks/family history are HAE red flags.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Angioedema of the right hand (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angioedema

teaching_point: Lingual angioedema (acquired C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency) — tongue/airway swelling is an emergency; antihistamines ineffective in bradykinin types.
dermnet_caption: Severe lingual angioedema in acquired C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Severe lingual angioedema in acquired C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/anaphylaxis

teaching_point: DermNet figure — HAE diagnostic algorithm: suspect when recurrent swellings without weals (abdominal attacks, family history, no antihistamine response); screen C4 then C1-INH level/function (specialist).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Clinical suspicion for hereditary angioedema (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hereditary-angioedema

teaching_point: Urticarial vasculitis — wheal-like plaques lasting >24 h, burn/hurt more than itch, may show purpura.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticarial vasculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/urticarial-vasculitis

teaching_point: Urticarial vasculitis in SLE — check complement/ANA; biopsy needed; refer to dermatology.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticarial vasculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/urticarial-vasculitis

teaching_point: Urticarial vasculitis — lesions resolve leaving bruise-like or brown pigment (unlike ordinary wheals).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticarial vasculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/urticarial-vasculitis

teaching_point: Urticarial vasculitis in skin of colour — residual hyperpigmentation is a useful clue.
dermnet_caption: Urticarial vasculitis in skin of colour
